PREMIERE316 STYLE-ONLY IMAGE REFERENCE CONTROL — V2
Asset ID: creature-white-dove
Workflow profile: 2P39X1 (2.39:1)
Reference mode: ART DIRECTION ONLY — NO SUBJECT OR DESIGN TRANSFER.

The loaded images are non-content style plates. The asset prompt below is the sole authority for subject, identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, wardrobe design, prop design, environment geometry, creatures, crowd population, pose, action, camera composition, wounds, blood placement, text, and all story content.

ALLOWED TRANSFER ONLY: overall palette; contrast curve; key/fill/rim relationship; volumetric-light behavior; atmosphere density; material highlight and shadow response; lens/exposure language; practical texture fidelity; cinematic depth; restrained film grain.

FORBIDDEN TRANSFER: faces or facial geometry; body identity or proportions; hairstyles; costume silhouettes; wounds or blood maps; weapons or props; architecture or set geography; creature designs; crowd layout; pose; framing; four-panel layout; lettering; logos; or any recognizable object from a reference, unless the asset prompt itself explicitly requests that exact element.

Crowd/creature guard: transfer only staging energy, chiaroscuro, atmosphere, and live-action realism. Do not reuse reference faces, bodies, demons, pleading hands, costumes, or crowd arrangement.

Active plate roles: warm-gold lighting and highlight rolloff; smoky umber shadow palette and ember atmosphere; abstract filmic tonal/material response and restrained grain.
When a reference conflicts with the row prompt, ignore the reference and obey the row prompt.

AUTHORITATIVE ASSET PROMPT
--------------------------
WHITE DOVE — PRODUCTION REFERENCE: CROWD OR CREATURE DESIGN, SCALE, VARIATION, AND CONTINUITY.

Photorealistic live-action production reference, physically coherent lighting, exact anatomy, clean hands, consistent scale and materials, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no borders, and no written or graphical elements.

Hero creature production reference of a single pure white dove in mid-flight, the sacred avian emblem of peace, the Holy Spirit, and resurrection freedom from the closing beat of JESUS: THE HARROWING OF HELL. This is an isolated hero bird asset for compositing into the desert-dawn finale, not a full landscape establishing shot—the dove itself is the subject and must read clearly at large scale.

Species and anatomy: a living rock dove (Columba livia) type rendered as an immaculate pure-white variant, fully photoreal live-action bird, never stylized illustration or CGI cartoon. Body length roughly life-scale for a dove (about twelve inches tip to tip when wings are folded; wingspan approximately twenty-four to twenty-eight inches when fully extended). Compact rounded head with a short slender pale-pink to warm-flesh beak, tiny dark nostrils, and a soft cere. Large, dark, liquid-black eyes with a thin pale orbital ring and gentle intelligent gaze directed slightly upward toward the new light. Smooth unbroken white plumage covering crown, nape, mantle, breast, and underparts—no gray bars, no black wing markings, no feral street-pigeon dirt. Individual flight feathers visible at the trailing edge of each wing: primary and secondary remiges slightly translucent where dawn light rakes through the barbs, soft downy coverts near the body, clean pure-white rectrices of the fanned tail. Delicate pinkish-gray feet drawn close to the body in flight posture, thin scaly legs, no rings or bands. Feathers hold fine directional grain, subtle overlapping structure, and micro-shadow between layers; the breast shows soft rounded volume with gentle subsurface scattering where warm light hits the down.

Pose and action—exact screenplay moment: a single dove flies upward into the new light after the fissure has sealed. Wings are captured at a powerful mid-upstroke or early downstroke, both wings fully extended and slightly cupped, primaries separated just enough to show individual feather tips against the sky. Body angled diagonally upward, head leading toward the upper frame, tail slightly fanned for balance. The motion freezes a graceful, purposeful ascent—not frantic flapping, not gliding hang—evoking liberation, the end of bondage, and the first breath of peace after Hell’s defeat. No flock, no second bird, no nest, no branch; only this solitary white dove rising alone.

Environment context (supporting, softly held back): the desert dawn of the final beat. Far below and out of sharp focus, a vast Judean wilderness of pale sand, soft dunes, and sealed earth where the vertical wound into Hell once opened—now smooth, peaceful, and closed. Horizon bands of residual deep purple and bruised night yielding to brilliant gold as the sun lifts. Extremely shallow depth of field keeps the dove razor-sharp while the desert floor and distant hills melt into creamy bokeh discs of amber and rose. Atmosphere is clean and quiet: a faint veil of golden dust motes or fine dawn haze catching god rays; no smoke from Hell, no ash, no blue torch light, no fortress architecture. Optional soft rim of residual divine radiance from the sealed fissure may glow as a low golden spill at the bottom of the frame, never overpowering the bird.

Lighting: warm natural dawn key from the rising sun, approximately 4500K to 5500K, hitting the underside and leading edges of the wings with honey-amber brilliance so each white feather reads luminous rather than flat paper-white. Soft fill from the pale sky above. Thin golden rim light along the wing tips and crown separates the pure white plumage from the bright sky without clipping. Specular micro-glints on the dark eye and the wet-looking beak tip. Volumetric god rays behind or beside the bird, faint and ethereal, suggesting the last triumphant spill of divine light from the sealed earth. Color grade: warm golden tones replacing the film’s earlier cold blues and hell crimsons—palette of pure white, soft cream feather shadows, amber, rose-gold, and residual dawn purple at the extreme edges of the sky. No cold cyan, no red underglow, no obsidian hell palette on this asset.

Camera and framing: photoreal cinematic production reference, anamorphic 2.39:1 widescreen sensibility even if the bird is centered as a hero subject. Medium-telephoto compression feel, roughly 85mm to 135mm equivalent, placing the dove large in frame with intimate feather detail while keeping the desert as soft environmental context. Slight low-to-high angle looking upward so the bird ascends into open sky—reverent, hopeful, liberating. Shallow DOF with the plane of focus locked on the head and near wing; far wing and tail may fall into gentle softness for dimensional realism. Natural motion-freeze sharpness on the body; optional micro motion blur only at the extreme primary tips if it serves realism, never smear. Clean production still language: no film grain overload, no heavy vignette, no borders.

Texture and atmosphere: every feather barb and vane readable in the sharp zones; soft bloom of dawn haze; tiny airborne dust particles catching light; dry desert air, no rain, no fog of death. Sacred biblical-epic tone—peaceful, triumphant, quiet after the storm. Continuity locks for compositing: pure white dove only; solitary; flying upward into new light; desert-dawn color world after Hell’s transformation; matches the last-frame dawn-after-victory guide where this bird rises as the emblem of resurrection and freedom. No modern objects, no cages, no bird feeders, no power lines, no buildings, no people in this isolated reference, no logos, no readable text, no watermarks, no captions, no UI, no borders. Photoreal live-action bird only—not illustration, not anime, not plastic CGI, not a plaster religious statue. One living white dove, ascending alone into the gold of a new day.
